boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named public-facing destinations along corridors in Trinity College’s practical Hartford orbit, each with a documented reason to visit.

cards.title: Pope Park: courts and pond
cards.subtitle: Park Street / Pope Park Drive corridor
cards.notes: Enter from Pope Park Drive and use the documented pond, athletic fields, or basketball courts for an outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A 79-acre city park with several active recreation features.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Hartford identifies Pope Park at 30 Pope Park Drive and lists athletic fields, a pond, basketball courts, and a recreation center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; consult the City for facility availability.

cards.title: Park Street Library @ the Lyric: browse and reset
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 603 Park Street during posted branch hours to browse, use library services, or check the program calendar.
cards.short_summary: A Hartford Public Library branch in the Lyric building.
cards.evidence_claim: Hartford Public Library lists Park Street Library @ the Lyric at 603 Park Street and provides current branch hours.
cards.source_title: Park Street Library @ the Lyric – Hartford Public Library
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Thursday 9:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; Friday 9:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: Parkville Market: food-hall stop
cards.subtitle: Park Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the food hall at 1400 Park Street when you want multiple vendor options in one documented destination.
cards.short_summary: A food-hall destination with vendors, pop-up shops, and live entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: Parkville Market lists its Hartford food hall at 1400 Park Street and says it hosts live entertainment and pop-up shops.
cards.source_title: Parkville Market – Find Us & Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Food and vendor purchases may be required; verify individual vendor hours before going.

cards.title: Camp Field Library: historic branch stop
cards.subtitle: Campfield Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit the branch at 30 Campfield Avenue during posted hours for a quiet, public library destination off campus.
cards.short_summary: Hartford Public Library’s first property-owned branch building.
cards.evidence_claim: Hartford Public Library states that Camp Field Library is at 30 Campfield Avenue and that its present building opened in 1937.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Thursday 9:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; Friday 9:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: Goodwin Park: trails and courts
cards.subtitle: Maple Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Start at the Maple Avenue entrance and choose a documented trail, fitness circuit, court, or picnic area for daylight recreation.
cards.short_summary: A 237-acre Hartford–Wethersfield park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Hartford lists Goodwin Park at 1192 Maple Avenue with trails, a fitness circuit, courts, a playscape, and picnic areas.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; some facilities or seasonal activities may have separate rules.

cards.title: Colt Park: paved walking trails
cards.subtitle: Wethersfield Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter at 130 Wethersfield Avenue and follow the park’s documented paved walking trails past its historic landscape features.
cards.short_summary: A historic 114-acre park with paved trails and sports facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Hartford lists Colt Park at 130 Wethersfield Avenue, notes its National Register listing, and identifies paved walking trails.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; check local notices for field, pool, or event access.

cards.title: Cedar Hill Cemetery: memorial grounds walk
cards.subtitle: Fairfield Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter through the Fairfield Avenue main gate and follow the visitor guidance while exploring the cemetery’s memorial grounds.
cards.short_summary: Publicly accessible memorial grounds with visitor materials at the entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Cedar Hill Cemetery Foundation states that the public may explore its memorial grounds through the main gate at 453 Fairfield Avenue.
cards.source_title: Plan a Visit – Cedar Hill Cemetery Foundation
cards.access_notes: Gates are listed as daily 7 a.m.–8 p.m. April–September and 7 a.m.–5 p.m. otherwise; respect cemetery rules.

cards.title: Hyland and Rocky Ridge: field-side recreation
cards.subtitle: New Britain Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the New Britain Avenue entrance for the documented ball fields, courts, playground, or turf field; stay within public areas.
cards.short_summary: A city park with active recreation facilities and a Trinity College land-history connection.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Hartford lists Hyland and Rocky Ridge Park at 391 New Britain Avenue and notes fields, courts, a playground, and an artificial turf field.
cards.source_title: Hyland and Rocky Ridge Park – City of Hartford
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; facilities may be reserved or unavailable during maintenance.

cards.title: Dwight Library: oldest branch
cards.subtitle: New Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit 7 New Park Avenue during posted hours for a library stop with a documented branch history dating to 1907.
cards.short_summary: Hartford Public Library’s oldest branch, now located in Parkville Elementary School.
cards.evidence_claim: Hartford Public Library identifies Dwight as its oldest branch, established in 1907, and lists its location at 7 New Park Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Thursday 9:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; Friday 9:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.entity_name: Connecticut Museum of Culture and History
cards.title: Connecticut Museum: gallery and research stop
cards.subtitle: Elizabeth Street / Asylum Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Plan an exhibit visit at One Elizabeth Street, or reserve research-center time if you want to work with its family-history resources.
cards.short_summary: A Hartford museum with exhibitions and the appointment-based Waterman Research Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Connecticut Museum of Culture and History is at One Elizabeth Street and offers exhibitions plus the Waterman Research Center by appointment.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit – Connecticut Museum of Culture and History
cards.access_notes: Museum hours are Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Thursday until 8 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; admission is generally ticketed.
